akhfash:12-12.t:
He said ﴿وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌ وَاعِيَةٌ﴾ because you say "وَعَتْ ذاكَ أذُنِي" ("my ear retained that") and "وَعَاهُ سَمْعِي" ("my hearing retained it"), and "أَوْعَيْتُ الزادَ" ("I put the provisions into a container") and "أَوْعَيْتُ المَتاعَ" ("I packed away the goods"), as the poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-first verse cited as evidence]:
[الخَيْرُ يَبْقَى وإِنْ طالَ الزَّمانُ بِهِ] * والشَرُّ أَخْبَثُ ما أَوْعَيْتَ مِنْ زادِ
(Good endures, however long time passes over it, and evil is the foulest provision you can pack away.)

akhfash:13-13.t: And He said ﴿فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ﴾ (in the nominative) because the verb fell on "the blast" (النفخة), since there was no nominative noun before it. «[Translator's note: i.e., نَفْخَةٌ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive verb نُفِخَ.]»

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿وَٱلْمَلَكُ عَلَىٰ أَرْجَآئِهَآ﴾: its singular is "الرَّجَا", and it is maqṣūr (ending in a short alif).

akhfash:36-36.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ﴾: He made it — and Allah knows best — from "الغَسْل" (washing) and added the yāʾ and the nūn, in the manner of "عُفْرِين" and "كُفْرِين".

akhfash:47-47.t: And He said ﴿فَمَا مِنكُمْ مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَاجِزِينَ﴾ according to the meaning, because the meaning of "أحَد" (anyone) is the meaning of a group.

daas-irab:2-3.t: ﴿الْحَاقَّةُ﴾ first mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مَا﴾ second mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْحَاقَّةُ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ, and the clause «الحاقة..» is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿وَما أَدْراكَ﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ, and a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar of ما, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿مَا الْحَاقَّةُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the second object of أدراك.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَعادٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ثمود. ﴿بِالْقارِعَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كذبت.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿أما﴾ a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl). ﴿ثَمُودُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فَأُهْلِكُوا﴾ the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِالطَّاغِيَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause of أما is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا عادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا﴾ the i'rab of its like has preceded. ﴿بِرِيحٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿صَرْصَرٍ عاتِيَةٍ﴾ two adjectives (ṣifa) of ريح.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿سَخَّرَها﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿سَبْعَ لَيالٍ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf), annexed to ليال; the clause is a third adjective (ṣifa) of ريح. ﴿وَثَمانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to سبع ليال. ﴿حُسُوماً﴾ an adjective of سبع ليال. ﴿فَتَرَى﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿ترى الْقَوْمَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿صَرْعى﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجازُ﴾ kaʾanna, its noun and its predicate. ﴿نَخْلٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿خاوِيَةٍ﴾ an adjective of أعجاز; the clause is a second ḥāl.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿هل﴾ an interrogative particle whose meaning is negation. ﴿تَرى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿باقِيَةٍ﴾ genitive (majrūr) in form by the redundant min, accusative (manṣūb) in position as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ترى; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وَجاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ conjoined to فرعون. ﴿قَبْلَهُ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿وَالْمُؤْتَفِكاتُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِالْخاطِئَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb جاء.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿فَعَصَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَسُولَ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَخَذَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَخْذَةً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿رابِيَةً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of أخذة; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya). ﴿طَغَى الْماءُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿حَمَلْناكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِي الْجارِيَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause «إن..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿لِنَجْعَلَها﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl), and hā is its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تذكرة. ﴿تَذْكِرَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to the verb حملناكم. ﴿وَتَعِيَها﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نجعلها. ﴿أُذُنٌ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿واعِيَةٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿إذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive. ﴿نُفِخَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿فِي الصُّورِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿نَفْخَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿واحِدَةٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of نفخة; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وَحُمِلَتِ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿الْأَرْضُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿وَالْجِبالُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الأرض; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَدُكَّتا﴾ a passive past verb, and the alif is the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿دَكَّةً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿واحِدَةً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of دكة; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:15-16.t: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and an adverb of time annexed to its like. ﴿وَقَعَتِ الْواقِعَةُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَانْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَهِيَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿هي﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to its like. ﴿واهِيَةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate).

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وَالْمَلَكُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلى أَرْجائِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to ربك. ﴿فَوْقَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ يوم is an adverb of time annexed to its like. ﴿ثَمانِيَةٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent) of يحمل; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ يوم is an adverb of time annexed to its like. ﴿تُعْرَضُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لا تَخْفى﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿خافِيَةٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿أما﴾ a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أُوتِيَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿كِتابَهُ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِيَمِينِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿فَيَقُولُ﴾ the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ من. ﴿هاؤُمُ﴾ a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr). ﴿اقْرَؤُا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿كِتابِيَهْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the hāʾ is for pausing (hāʾ al-sakt); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿ظَنَنْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إني, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَنِّي مُلاقٍ﴾ anna, its noun and its predicate. ﴿حِسابِيَهْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ملاق, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the hāʾ is for pausing (hāʾ al-sakt); the interpreted maṣdar formed from anna, its noun and its predicate stands in place of the two objects of ظننت.

daas-irab:21-23.t: ﴿فَهُوَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿هو﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي عِيشَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿راضِيَةٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of عيشة; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي جَنَّةٍ﴾ badal (substitute) of His words في عيشة. ﴿عالِيَةٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a second adjective of جنة.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿كُلُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf). ﴿وَاشْرَبُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to كلوا. ﴿هَنِيئاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) هنيئا. ﴿أَسْلَفْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿فِي الْأَيَّامِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْخالِيَةِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of الأيام.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِشِمالِهِ فَيَقُولُ﴾ see verse 19. ﴿يا﴾ a particle of alerting (tanbīh). ﴿لَيْتَنِي﴾ a particle resembling the verb, the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is its noun. ﴿لَمْ أُوتَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿كِتابِيَهْ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the hāʾ is for pausing (hāʾ al-sakt); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of layta, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:26-29.t: ﴿وَلَمْ أَدْرِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حِسابِيَهْ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the hāʾ is for pausing (hāʾ al-sakt); the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of أدري. ﴿يا﴾ a particle of alerting (tanbīh). ﴿لَيْتَها﴾ layta and its noun. ﴿كانَتِ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْقاضِيَةَ﴾ khabar of كانت; the verbal clause is the khabar of layta, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿ما أَغْنى﴾ mā is negative, and a past verb. ﴿عَنِّي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مالِيَهْ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿هَلَكَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَنِّي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سُلْطانِيَهْ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:30-32.t: ﴿خُذُوهُ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of an implied saying (maqūl li-qawl muqaddar). ﴿فَغُلُّوهُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to خذوه. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿الْجَحِيمَ﴾ accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿صَلُّوهُ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) اسلكوه. ﴿ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of سلسلة. ﴿ذِراعاً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿فَاسْلُكُوهُ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ كانَ﴾ inna and its noun, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir). ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا يَحُضُّ﴾ negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلى طَعامِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْمِسْكِينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:35-37.t: غسلين: the pus (ṣadīd) of the people of the Fire. ﴿فَلَيْسَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of laysa. ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿هاهُنا﴾ hā is for alerting (tanbīh). ﴿هنا﴾ a demonstrative in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb of place. ﴿حَمِيمٌ﴾ the postponed noun of laysa; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿طَعامٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to حميم. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of طعام. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَأْكُلُهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿الْخاطِؤُنَ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is an adjective of غسلين.

daas-irab:38-40.t: ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِما تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَقَوْلُ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿قول رَسُولٍ﴾ khabar (predicate) of inna, annexed to رسول. ﴿كَرِيمٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the nominal clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:41-41.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾ negative, operating like laysa. ﴿هُوَ﴾ its noun. ﴿بِقَوْلِ﴾ genitive (majrūr) in form by the redundant (zāʾida) bāʾ, accusative (manṣūb) in position as the khabar (predicate) of mā. ﴿شاعِرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿ما﴾ redundant. ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:42-42.t: ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation. ﴿بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بقول شاعر; the i'rab of the like of what follows it has preceded.

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿تَنْزِيلٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْ رَبِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنزيل. ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:44-44.t: ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional, not making jussive. ﴿تَقَوَّلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿بَعْضَ الْأَقاوِيلِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to الأقاويل; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:45-46.t: ﴿لَأَخَذْنا﴾ the lām occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿بِالْيَمِينِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction, and the clause ﴿لَقَطَعْنا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:47-47.t: ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ أَحَدٍ﴾ genitive (majrūr) in form by the redundant (zāʾida) min, nominative (marfūʿ) in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿حاجِزِينَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of أحد.

daas-irab:48-48.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿تذكرة﴾ khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تذكرة; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the response to the oath.

daas-irab:49-49.t: ﴿وَإِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَنَعْلَمُ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ the fronted khabar of anna. ﴿مُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ its postponed noun; the interpreted maṣdar formed from anna and what follows it is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), standing in place of the two objects of نعلم.

daas-irab:50-50.t: The i'rab of its like has preceded in verse 48.

daas-irab:51-52.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿حق الْيَقِينِ﴾ khabar (predicate) of inna, annexed to اليقين; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَسَبِّحْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِاسْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position.

farraa:1-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْحَاقَّةُ مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ﴾.
Al-Ḥāqqa [204/b] is the Resurrection; it is so called because in it are the reward and the requital. The Arabs say: لما عرفت الحقة منى هربت (when you knew the truth of the matter from me, you fled), and [also] الحاقة; the two have one meaning.
Al-Ḥāqqa is nominative by virtue of the wonderment expressed at its mention, as in your saying: الحاقة ماهى؟ (The Reality — what is it?). The second refers back to the first. Likewise His saying: ﴿وأصْحَابُ الْيَمِينِ مَا أصْحَابُ الْيَمِين﴾ and ﴿القارِعَةُ، مَا الْقَارِعَةُ﴾: its meaning is: What thing is al-Qāriʿa? So ما is in the position of the nominative by the second القارعة, and the first is nominative by the whole clause [following it]. And al-Qāriʿa is also the Resurrection.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَّابِيَةً﴾.
[I.e.] an exceeding seizure, as you say أربيتَ (you took usury) when someone takes more than he gave of gold and silver; you say: قد أربيت فَرَبا رِباك (you have taken usury, and your usury has grown).

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً﴾: that We might make the ship a reminder for you: an admonition.
His saying: ﴿وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌ وَاعِيَةٌ﴾.
He is saying: that every ear might retain it, so that it may be an admonition for those who come after.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا﴾. He did not say فدككن, because He treated the mountains as a single thing, just as He said: ﴿أنّ السَّمَاواتِ والأَرْضَ كانَتَا رَتْقاً﴾ and did not say: كنّ رتقا. Had it been said here: وحملت الأرض والجبال فدكَّت, it would be correct, because the mountains and the earth are like one thing.
His saying: ﴿دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾.
Its دكّ is its being shaken by earthquake.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱنشَقَّتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَهِيَ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاهِيَةٌ﴾: its frailty (wahy) is its splitting apart.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمَانِيَةٌ﴾: it is said: eight parts out of nine parts of the angels.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it with yāʾ, and the people after him read it with tāʾ: (لا تخفى); both are correct. It is like His saying: ﴿وأَخذَ الذينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ and وأخذت.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ﴾.
It came down concerning Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Asad; he was a believer, and his brother al-Aswad was an unbeliever, and concerning him there came down: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِشِمَالِهِ﴾.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنِّي ظَنَنتُ أَنِّي مُلاَقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ﴾, that is: I knew. It is of the knowledge of what is not seen; that has been explained in more than one place.
[Translator's note: «يعابَن» is as printed, for «يُعايَن» ("seen with the eyes").]

farraa:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿فِى عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ﴾: in which there is contentment. The Arabs [216/a] say: هذا ليل نائم (a sleeping night), سر كاتم (a concealing secret) and ماء دافق (gushing water), making it an active participle when it is originally a passive participle. That is because they intend praise or blame, and they say it not according to the structure of the verb. If it were an explicit verbal [sense], that would not be said of it, because it is not permissible to call the striker مضروب (struck) nor the struck ضارب (striker), since there is neither praise nor blame in it.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰلَيْتَهَا كَانَتِ ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ﴾.
He is saying: would that the first death had been the one after which I was never brought to life.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ﴾.
It is mentioned that it enters the unbeliever's rear and comes out of his head; that is his being threaded into it. The meaning is: then thread a chain into him; but the Arabs say: أدخلت رأسى فى القلنسوة (I put my head into the cap) and أدخلتها فى رأسى (I put it on my head). And of the ring it is said: الخاتم لا يدخل فى يدى (the ring does not go into my hand), while it is the hand that goes into it — this is from al-Farrāʾ's statement.
Abū ʿAbd Allāh [Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm] said: and the leather sock (khuff) is like that. They allowed this because its meaning is unclear to no one, so they made light of whatever of that ran on their tongues.

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ طَعَامٌ إِلاَّ مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ﴾: it is said that it is the pus that flows from the people of the Fire.

farraa:44-45.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ ٱلأَقَاوِيلِ﴾: He is saying: if Muḥammad ﷺ had fabricated against Us what he was not commanded, ﴿لأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِٱلْيَمِينِ﴾: with strength and power.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَا مِنكُمْ مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَاجِزِينَ﴾.
أحد may be used for a plural and for a singular. Al-Aʿmash mentioned in a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: (Spoils were not made lawful for any [أحد] of the black-headed except for your Prophet ﷺ), so he made أحد stand in the place of a plural. And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لاَ نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ﴾, and this is plural, because بين applies only to two or more.
[Translator's note: «ألم تَحل» is as printed; the sense requires «لم تَحِلّ» ("were not made lawful").]

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُوماً﴾.
الحسوم means succession: when a thing follows on continuously so that its beginning is not cut off from its end, it is called حسوم. It is taken — and Allah knows best — from حسم الداء (cauterising a disease), when the sufferer is cauterised: he is cauterised with an iron, and then that is repeated on him in succession.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ تَرَىٰ لَهُم مِّن بَاقِيَةٍ﴾: [i.e.] any survival (baqāʾ). It is also said: Do you see any one of them remaining (bāqiyan)? All of that is permissible and good in Arabic.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَآءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَن قَبْلَهُ﴾.
ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and the people of Medina read it: (ومن قَبله), and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and al-Ḥasan, or Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān — al-Farrāʾ was unsure — read: (ومن قِبَلهُ) with kasra on the qāf. In the reading of Ubayy it is: (وجاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ ومَن مَعَه), and in the reading of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī: "ومن تِلْقَاءَه"; these two are evidence for whoever reads the qāf with kasra, because they are like your saying: Pharaoh came and his followers. And whoever says ومن قَبْلَهُ means the disobedient nations before him.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَاتُ بِالْخَاطِئَةِ﴾.
[I.e.] those who were overturned because of their sin.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa
Meccan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿الحاقَّةُ﴾ ﴿ما الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 2] ("The Inevitable Reality! What is the Inevitable Reality?"). The first is nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); «ما» is also nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the second «الحاقَّةُ» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما». The [element] referring back to «ما» is the second «الحاقَّةُ», on the implied sense "What is it?" The meaning is to magnify its importance, while the wording is that of a question, as when you say: «زَيْدٌ، ما هُوَ؟» ("Zayd — what is he?!"), in the sense of magnifying his standing, whether in praise or in blame. «الحاقَّة» is the Hour and the Resurrection; it was called «الحاقَّة» because it makes real (taḥiqqu) everything a person does, good or evil. Likewise ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 3] ("And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?") means: "What thing has made you know what the Inevitable Reality is?" The position of «ما» is nominative even though it comes after «أدْراكَ», because what is in the form of a question is not governed by what precedes it; the meaning is: "What has made you know what thing the Inevitable Reality is?!"

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا لَمّا طَغى الماءُ حَمَلْناكم في الجارِيَةِ﴾ ("When the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship"). The meaning of «طَغى الماءُ» is: it swelled and rose. The meaning of «الجارِيَة» is: the ship of Noah (peace be upon him), and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿لِنَجْعَلَها لَكم تَذْكِرَةً﴾ ("that We might make it a reminder for you") means: that We might make this deed a reminder for you, i.e. the drowning of the people of Noah and the rescue of him and the believers with him.
And His saying: ﴿وَتَعِيَها أُذُنٌ واعِيَةٌ﴾ ("and that a retaining ear might retain it") means: an ear that keeps what it has heard and acts upon it, i.e. so that the hearer keeps what he has heard and acts upon it. Of everything you keep within yourself you say «قَدْ وعَيْتُهُ»; one says «قَدْ وعَيْتُ العِلْمَ» ("I have retained the knowledge") and «وَعَيْتُ»; and of what you keep in something other than yourself you say «أوْعَيْتُهُ»; one says «أوْعَيْتُ المَتاعَ في الوِعاءِ» ("I put the goods away in the container").
[Translator's note: the source has «و"وَعَيْتُ"، قُلْتَ وتَقُولُ», which appears garbled; translated as far as it is intelligible.]

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا نُفِخَ في الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ واحِدَةٌ﴾ ("Then when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast"). The reading is with the nominative in ﴿نَفْخَةٌ﴾, as [the subject of a verb] whose agent is not named (i.e. nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). Al-Akhfash mentioned «نَفْخَةً واحِدَةً» in the accusative, and did not mention whether it was read so or not. It is permissible in Arabic on the basis that your saying «فِي الصُّورِ» stands in place of the deputy agent; you say «فِي الصُّورِ نَفْخًا», so «فِي الصُّورِ» is genitive in its wording, and the meaning is "the Trumpet was blown with a single blast" — this is for whoever puts «نَفْخَةً واحِدَةً» in the accusative. Whoever puts it in the nominative, it is on the meaning: "a single blast was blown in the Trumpet". As for the masculine «نُفِخَ»: had it been «نُفِخَتْ في الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ» it would have been permissible; [but the masculine is used] because it is a non-real feminine, so making it masculine is permissible, since «النَّفْخَة» and «النَّفْخ» have one meaning. Similar to it is ﴿فَمَن جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِن رَبِّهِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 275] ("So whoever an admonition from his Lord comes to"); the meaning is the meaning of «الوَعْظ» (admonishing), while He said in another place: ﴿قَدْ جاءَتْكم مَوْعِظَةٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [Yūnus: 57] ("There has come to you an admonition from your Lord").

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿وانْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ فَهي يَوْمَئِذٍ واهِيَةٌ﴾ ("And the sky will be split, for that Day it will be frail"). Of anything that has become very weak one says «قَدْ وهى، فَهو واهٍ». And «وِاهِيَةٌ» is also permissible, with imāla (inclination) of the alif and the wāw because of the kasra of the hāʾ.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿والمَلَكُ عَلى أرْجائِها﴾ ("And the angels will be on its edges"): the meaning is "the angels on its sides". The rajā of everything is its side; it is a maqṣūr noun (ending in short alif), its dual is «رَجَوانِ» and its plural «أرْجاء».
﴿وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهم يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمانِيَةٌ﴾ ("And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day"): it is narrated: eight angels, their feet in the depths of the seventh earth and the Throne above their heads, while they, with heads bowed, glorify [Allah].
﴿فَأمّا مَن أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ اقْرَءُوا كِتابِيَهْ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 19] ("As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Here, read my record!"): it is narrated: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, creation will be presented three times: in two of them there will be argument, excuse-making and rebuke, and in the third the records will be scattered, and the successful one will take his record in his right hand and the ruined one his record in his left." ﴿هاؤُمُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 19] is an imperative for a group, equivalent to «هاكُمْ» ("here, take!"). You say to one man «هاءَ يا رَجُلُ», to two «هاؤُما يا رَجُلانِ», to three «هاؤُمُ يا رِجالُ», to a woman «هاءِ يا امْرَأةُ» with kasra on the hamza, to two [women] «هاؤُما», and to a group of women «هاؤُنَّ». There are three dialectal forms of this, which I have mentioned in a book other than [this] book on the Qur'an.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿إنِّي ظَنَنْتُ أنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ﴾ ("Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account") means: "I was certain that I would be brought to account and raised." As for «كِتابِيَهْ» and «حِسابِيَهْ», the proper way is to pause on these hāʾs and not to read them in connection, because they were brought in for the pause. Some people dropped them in connected reading, but I do not like to contradict the Muṣḥaf, nor to read with the hāʾ retained in connected reading. These are verse-endings, so the proper way is to pause at them; and likewise His saying: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 10] ("And what will make you know what it is?").

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ﴾ ("its clusters hanging near") means: they draw near to whoever wants them; neither distance nor thorns prevent him from reaching them.
And His saying: ﴿فِي الأيّامِ الخالِيَةِ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 24] ("in the days gone by") means: in the days that passed for them.
His saying: ﴿صَلُّوهُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 31] ("burn him"): the meaning is "make him roast in the Fire".

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ﴾ ("my authority has perished from me") means: "my argument has gone from me". «السُّلْطان» is the argument (ḥujja); likewise rulers were called «سَلاطِين», because they are the ones by whom the argument and rights are upheld.

zajjaj:36-36.t: His saying ﴿مِن غِسْلِينٍ﴾ ("of ghislīn") means: of the pus of the people of the Fire; its derivation is from what is washed off (yanghasilu) their bodies.

zajjaj:4-4.t: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned those who denied the Inevitable Reality, the Hour, the matter of the raising and the Resurrection, and what befell them, as an admonition to the community of Muḥammad ﷺ, and said: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وعادٌ بِالقارِعَةِ﴾ ("Thamūd and ʿĀd denied the Striking Calamity"), i.e. the Resurrection.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿قَلِيلا ما تُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("little is it that you believe") and ﴿قَلِيلا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 42] ("little is it that you take heed"): «ما» is emphatic and is void (laghw) as regards i'rab; the meaning is «قَلِيلًا تُؤْمِنُونَ» and «قَلِيلًا تَذَكَّرُونَ».

zajjaj:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿تَنْـزِيلٌ مِن رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ ("A revelation from the Lord of the worlds"): it is nominative by an implied «هُوَ» ("it is"), indicated by His saying ﴿وَما هو بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 41] ("and it is not the word of a poet"), i.e. "It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds."

zajjaj:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الأقاوِيلِ﴾ ("And had he fabricated against Us some sayings"): He means by it the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
﴿لأخَذْنا مِنهُ بِاليَمِينِ﴾ ("We would have seized him by the right hand"), i.e. with power and strength. Al-Shammākh said:
؎إذا ما رايَةٌ رُفِعَتْ لِمَجْدٍ ∗∗∗ تَلَقّاها عَرابَةٌ بِاليَمِينِ
(Whenever a banner is raised for glory, ʿArāba receives it with the right hand.)

zajjaj:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنهُ الوَتِينَ﴾ ("then We would have cut his aorta"): «الوَتِين» is the main artery by which the heart is suspended (niyāṭ al-qalb).

zajjaj:47-47.t: ﴿فَما مِنكم مِن أحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ﴾ ("And none of you could have shielded him"): «حاجِزِينَ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أحَد», and «أحَد» here has the meaning of "all"; the meaning is: "There is no group among you who could hold [Us] back from him."

zajjaj:5-5.t:
﴿فَأمّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطّاغِيَةِ﴾ ("As for Thamūd, they were destroyed by al-ṭāghiya"). The meaning of ﴿بِالطّاغِيَةِ﴾ according to the lexicographers is: by their transgression (ṭughyān); the pattern fāʿila sometimes comes with the meaning of maṣdars (verbal nouns), such as «عافِيَة» (well-being) and «عاقِبَة» (outcome). But what the meaning of the verse points to — and Allah knows best — is that they were destroyed by the overwhelming (ṭāghiya) earthquake, just as He said: ﴿وَأمّا عادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عاتِيَةٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 6] ("And as for ʿĀd, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind"). Of a mighty thing one says «عاتٍ» and «عاتِيَة»; likewise they were destroyed by the ṭāghiya. The evidence for describing a mighty thing with ṭughyān is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا لَمّا طَغى الماءُ حَمَلْناكم في الجارِيَةِ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 11] ("When the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship"); He described the water with ṭughyān because it exceeded the measure in abundance. So likewise they were destroyed by the ṭāghiya, and Allah knows best.
And His saying: ﴿بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عاتِيَةٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 6] means: by a wind of very intense cold. «الصَّرْصَر» is intensity of cold, and «صَرْصَر» is [a wind] in which the cold repeats itself — just as you say «قَلْقَلْتُ الشَّيْءَ» and «أقْلَلْتُ الشَّيْءَ» when you lift a thing from its place, except that «قَلْقَلْتُهُ» means I moved it back and forth, i.e. I lifted it repeatedly, whereas «أقْلَلْتُهُ» means I lifted it, and there is no indication of repetition in it. Likewise «صَرْصَر» and «صَرّ», «صَلْصَل» and «صَلّ»: when you hear the sound of creaking not repeated, you say «قَدْ صَرَّ» and «صَلَّ»; and when you mean that the sound was repeated, you say «قَدْ صَلْصَلَ» and «صَرْصَرَ».

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَحَقُّ اليَقِينِ﴾ ("And indeed it is the truth of certainty"): the meaning is that the Qur'an, as certainty, is the very truth of certainty.

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ العَظِيمِ﴾ ("So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great"): «التَّسْبِيح» means declaring Allah free of evil, and declaring Him, the Exalted, transcendent.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿سَخَّرَها عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيالٍ وثَمانِيَةَ أيّامٍ حُسُومًا﴾ ("He imposed it upon them for seven nights and eight days, ḥusūman"). The meaning of ﴿سَخَّرَها عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ is: He kept it upon them as He willed. The meaning of ﴿حُسُومًا﴾ is "continuous", and they also said "successive". As for what the language requires, it is in the sense of "cutting them off completely (taḥsimuhum ḥusūman)", i.e. carrying them away and annihilating them.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَأنَّهم أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ خاوِيَةٍ﴾ ("as though they were the trunks of hollow palm trees"): «أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ» are the stumps of palm trees. «خاوِيَةٍ» was said of the palm trees because «نَخْل» is treated as both masculine and feminine; one says «هَذا نَخْلٌ حَسَنٌ» and «هَذِهِ نَخْلٌ حَسَنَةٌ». So «خاوِيَةٍ» is on the feminine, and He said in another place: ﴿أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 20] ("the trunks of uprooted palm trees").

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿وَجاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ ومَن قَبْلَهُ﴾ ("And Pharaoh came, and those before him"). It was also read «وَمَن قِبَلَهُ». Whoever says «وَمَن قِبَلَهُ», its meaning is: and his followers; and whoever says «وَمَن قَبْلَهُ», the meaning is: those who preceded him. ﴿والمُؤْتَفِكاتُ بِالخاطِئَةِ﴾ ("and the overturned cities, with sin"): «المُؤْتَفِكات» are those who were overturned (iʾtufikū) for their sins, i.e. destroyed for their sins, the greatest of which was ifk — lying concerning the matter of Allah — in that they disbelieved and denied the messengers; therefore they were called «مُؤْتَفِكُون». Likewise those with whom the earth was overturned (iʾtafakat), i.e. who were swallowed by it: its meaning is simply that it turned over with them, just as the liar turns the truth over into falsehood. The meaning of ﴿بِالخاطِئَةِ﴾ is: with the great error. The evidence that lying was among their greatest sins is His saying: ﴿فَعَصَوْا رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأخَذَهم أخْذَةً رابِيَةً﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 10] ("And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with an ever-increasing seizure"), because they denied their messengers. ﴿أخْذَةً رابِيَةً﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 10]: the meaning of ﴿رابِيَةً﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 10] is: exceeding [other] events.
